question: how many SugarCrepe pairs differ only in word order
method: lowercase, tokenise on [a-z0-9']+, compare multisets of the positive and negative caption
why_it_matters: for a bag-identical pair, any model whose text representation ignores word order assigns both captions the same score, so it lands at chance by construction. On the swap_* splits such a model cannot exceed chance however good its content representation is, and a swap score therefore does not separate content quality across that class of models.

examples.positive: Blue bathroom with two white towels hanging by the shower.
examples.negative: White bathroom with two blue towels hanging by the shower.

examples.positive: a brick building with a blue sign on it in front of a metal pole
examples.negative: a blue building with a brick sign on it in front of a metal pole.

examples.positive: A man in a red shirt rides a yellow surfboard on light blue water.
examples.negative: A man in a yellow shirt rides a red surfboard on light blue water.

examples.positive: A cat sits on its hind legs, and swats at the plant.
examples.negative: A cat sits on the plant, and swats at its hind legs.

examples.positive: A woman prepares a pizza while a man watches.
examples.negative: A man prepares a pizza while a woman watches.

examples.positive: Girls wash a motorcycle while men look on.
examples.negative: Men wash a motorcycle while girls look on.

scope: this is a property of the benchmark data alone. No model was run. It is not a defect: the swap splits are meant to probe word order. It is a caveat about how their scores read.
